text: dsh-tool-search 是一款面向 DSH Native Tool Mode 的工具发现插件，为每个 agent 提供独立的 tool_search。它按工具名称与描述进行词法排序，优先匹配精确名称，并用 BM25 返回有限数量的候选工具；被选中的工具会在后续请求中加载。插件将选择快照写入会话，以便恢复或分叉后继续使用，并保留 alwaysVisible 配置的全局工具。适合工具较多、希望按需发现和加载工具的 DSH 使用场景；无需额外 API 密钥或外部服务。

dsh-tool-search adds per-agent tool discovery to DSH Native Tool Mode. Agents search global tool names and descriptions with exact-name priority and BM25, then load selected tools for later requests. Session snapshots restore selections after resume or fork. It needs no API key or external service.
想让每个 DSH agent 只先看到少量常用工具，需要时再找其他工具。
工具太多导致请求携带的 schema 很长，能不能按需加载？
希望 agent 可以用自然语言描述能力来搜索可用工具。
让指定名称的工具始终可见，其余工具通过搜索再加载。
会话恢复后如何保留之前搜索选中的工具？
我想让多个 agent 各自维护独立的工具选择。
Can an agent discover tools by describing a capability and load matches on demand?
I want each agent to keep its own selected tools across session resume.
@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search 的功能「按描述搜索工具」：调用 tool_search 提交能力描述或工具名；插件以精确名称优先并按 BM25 对名称和说明排序，最多返回配置上限内的结果。
@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search 的功能「逐步加载匹配工具」：每个 agent 搜索后将命中工具加入自己的选择，并刷新工具限制；工具在后续模型请求中可见，受其他限制阻挡时标为 unavailable。
@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search 的功能「恢复会话中的工具选择」：插件读取最近的 tool-search/selection 会话事件，恢复排序后的工具选择；每次新增选择时保存完整快照，支持会话恢复或分叉。
@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search 的功能「设置始终可见工具」：通过 alwaysVisible 配置工具名称模式，星号可匹配任意字符；这些全局工具无需搜索即可保留在 agent 的允许列表中。
@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search 使用前须知：当前搜索只支持 Native Tool Mode；嵌套在 run_code 下的调用会报错，且搜索目录只包含全局工具。

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

An experimental external Native Tool Mode plugin for per-agent tool discovery and progressive schema disclosure. Each live agent sees one scope-local `tool_search` tool plus the global tools matched by `alwaysVisible`; other eligible global tools stay executable only after `tool_search` selects them. The plugin uses the existing `ctx.tools.restrict()` seam and does not change `agent-loop`.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search：This private repository is the plugin's source of truth. The package is unreleased and carries no compatibility promise. See the [scale benchmark report](docs/reports/2026-08-11-tool-search-benchmark.md) for keyless 10/30/50/100-tool results and the [design record](docs/design/2026-08-11-tool-search-progressive-disclosure.md) for the decision and trade-offs.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · Installation：The repository is private and the package is not published to an npm registry. Install a reviewed commit directly from GitHub with Git credentials and pnpm `11.7.0`; install it separately into every profile that should use tool search. The `-w` flag is required because a DSH profile is a pnpm workspace root:

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · Installation：```sh
dsh plugin --profile headless add -w github:dsh-external/dsh-tool-search#<reviewed-commit>
dsh plugin --profile web add -w github:dsh-external/dsh-tool-search#<reviewed-commit>
dsh --profile web --dump-config
```

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · Installation：The package's `dsh.bundle.patch` loads both the runtime plugin and its invariant companion. Profiles are independent; installing into `web` does not enable `headless`. `--dump-config` must show `tool-search` and `tool-search-invariant` before the profile is booted. Remove the bundle from one profile with `dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove -w @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search`.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · Config：```yaml
- id: tool-search
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search'
  config:
    alwaysVisible: [read_file, todo_*]

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `alwaysVisible` | `[]` | Global tool-name patterns that remain visible before search. Only `*` is a wildcard; every other character is literal. |
| `maxResults` | `5` | Largest allowed result limit for one search. |
| `maxQueryChars` | `512` | Largest trimmed query accepted in JavaScript characters. |

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · Config：Invalid positive-integer bounds, empty or whitespace-padded patterns, and repeated patterns fail at plugin load. A model may request a smaller `limit`, from `1` through `maxResults`; it cannot raise the deployment bound.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · Selection and safety：Search ranks exact callable names first, then name and description matches with deterministic BM25 scoring and code-point name tie-breaking. A successful expansion writes one `tool-search/selection` session event containing the trimmed query and the complete sorted selected-name set. Later events must be strict cumulative supersets; the invariant companion enforces the event shape and monotonic rule for live and restored sessions.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · Selection and safety：Each agent owns an independent selection and restriction. A resumed or forked session restores the latest selection before its first request. Installing the plugin after agents already exist attaches them; unloading it removes `tool_search` and lifts only its own restrictions.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · Selection and safety：This plugin never widens another filter. Existing creation-time restrictions, parent/subagent policy, scoped shadows, and other `ctx.tools.restrict()` calls still intersect after search, so a selected but independently denied tool reports `unavailable`. The initial catalog includes only globals already visible to that agent. Late global registrations such as MCP tools join the catalog only when the agent started with an unrestricted global view; an agent that started behind another restriction stays on its original eligible-name set. `alwaysVisible` is the explicit override for a known late name pattern.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · What the model sees：Every protected agent sees the following description even when no global tool is initially visible; the complete declaration lives in [`src/index.ts`](src/index.ts). The schema has `query` (required string) and `limit` (optional integer bounded by config). The tool is scope-local, so this plugin's global allow-list cannot hide it.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · Token effect：The fixed `tool_search` schema and the `alwaysVisible` schemas are paid on every request. Deferred tool schemas cost no request tokens until selected. A search result adds a small retained history entry; selected full schemas begin on the next request.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · KV Cache effect：The request prefix stays stable while the selected set and registry stay unchanged; selecting the same tool again does not change the schema list. The current registry emits newly visible global tools before the scope-local `tool_search`, so the serialized tool schemas after the first selection retain only about 2% of their initial prefix in the [keyless scale benchmark](docs/reports/2026-08-11-tool-search-benchmark.md). Functional behavior is unaffected, but strong KV Cache gains require the mainline to provide stable schema ordering or a formal deferred contribution seam. Tool registration, removal, or plugin lifecycle can also change the schema prefix.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · What the model sees：Matching results use the following concise format. No match renders `No matching tools found.` The canonical value also includes the trimmed `query`, ordered `tools` records, and `remainingDeferred`. `loaded` means the tool became visible, `already_loaded` means it was already visible, and `unavailable` means another restriction still blocks it. Full schemas are not copied into the result; they arrive through the next normal request header.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · Result example：```markdown
Tool search results:
- <tool_name>: <loaded|already_loaded|unavailable>
Remaining deferred tools: <count>.
```
@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · Token effect：Result size is bounded by `maxResults` and retained until compaction. The newly selected schemas then add their normal fixed per-request cost.
@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · KV Cache effect：The result appends after the reusable history prefix. The following request changes its schema prefix when at least one tool was newly selected.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · What the model sees：Blank or overlong queries, an out-of-range or non-integer `limit`, calls without the owning live agent, and nested Code Mode dispatch return ordinary tool errors. A failed call does not change the selection or append `tool-search/selection`.
@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · Token effect：The error result enters history as an ordinary tool result and is retained until compaction; it introduces no deferred tool schemas.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · KV Cache effect：The error result appends after the existing prefix and does not change the tool-schema prefix. If the same failure occurs again, it extends the request like any other new history.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **Native Tool Mode only.** Calls nested under `run_code` fail loud; Code Mode needs a separate SDK/search transport contract.
- **Lexical search only.** Exact names, name boosts, descriptions, and BM25 achieve 100% recall for exact name @1 and representative capability queries @5 in the keyless scale benchmark; this small fixed corpus does not represent ambiguous queries, multilingual queries, or real model-use quality. Embeddings and provider-native search remain deferred.
- **Global tools only.** Agent-scoped tools are already visible and never enter the deferred catalog. MCP resources and prompts are outside the tool registry and need their own consumer seams.
- **Conservative late-tool policy.** Any restricted initial global view freezes the eligible-name set, so a harmless later registration may stay undiscoverable unless `alwaysVisible` names it.
- **No namespace grouping.** Individual tool names remain the selection unit; large MCP servers may need a namespace-level result and load operation.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-search README · Development and verification：The checked-in `lib/` output is installable without rebuilding. The project `.npmrc` selects the private `@deepseek-ai/*` scope; pnpm 11 reads its `${NPM_TOKEN}` authentication mapping from the trusted user-level `~/.npmrc`. Set `NPM_TOKEN`, then run `pnpm install --ignore-scripts` and `pnpm run check`. The SDK packages are pinned to the reviewed `0.0.1-rc.2` set. Do not link a DSH source checkout into this repository. The optional benchmark also requires `DSH_TOOL_CATALOG_PATH` to name an exported DSH tool catalog. The `compat/` directory is an external compatibility fixture, not a source-development dependency.
